newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Strong support for opposition in Buenos Aires poll.
newsitem.headline: Strong support for opposition in Buenos Aires poll.

text.p: Most voters in the key Argentine province of Buenos Aires would opt for the likely candidate of the center-left Frepaso in mid-term congressional elections, according to a poll Wednesday.

Some 51.4 percent of those surveyed responded positively when asked if they would vote for Senator Graciela Fernandez Meijide, according to the survey by private pollsters Rouvier y Asociados printed by the El Cronista newspaper.
Another 31.7 percent said they would not vote for her in the October elections, and 16.9 percent said they did not know.
Buenos Aires province is Argentina's most populous electoral district and is home to about 40 percent of the country's voters, although it does not include the center of the city of Buenos Aires.

Fernandez Meijide, one of the leading figures of Argentina's opposition, has been proposed by Frepaso leader Carlos Alvarez as the province-wide candidate in Buenos Aires for the lower house Chamber of Deputies.

Frepaso has been negotiating a possible alliance with the Radical Party to contest Buenos Aires province. But El Cronista quoted Frepaso officials saying that the latest poll results make them think they may not need the Radicals and can beat the governing Peronist Party on their own.
The poll of 500 respondents was carried out in January. El Cronista did not print the margin of error.
